newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Cosumar starts up $10.6 mln sugar plant.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Cosumar starts up $10.6 mln sugar plant.

text.p: Morocco's leading sugar refiner Cosumar has started operating a new refining unit worth $10.6 million to improve quality and increase production, a manager with the company said on Thursday.

"The new sugar plant is now 100 percent operational...It will enable Cosumar to improve its quality products and increase production capacity to 720,000 tonnes per year," the manager, who asked not to be named, said.
Cosumar, a subsidiary of Morocco's largest conglomerate ONA Group, has annual production of 670,000 tonnes.
"More than 100 million dirhams were invested in the new refinery unit as part of continuing investments to upgrade the sugar sector," the manager added.
He declined to give other details about the Casablanca unit.
A market analyst said the 100 million dirhams was "a first tranche" which would be followed by other investments to expand Cosumar refining activities.

ONA's chairman Fouad Filali told a shareholders' meeting on Wednesday that "Cosumar is committed to ... improvement of its competitiveness and consolidating market shares to face the impact of commmodity liberalisation."

The Moroccan authorities announced the liberalisation of the commodity market in July 1996 but "instruments and mechanisms" of effective liberalisation have not been put in place as promised, Filali said.
Cosumar, which holds the monopoly on importing and refining raw sugar, bought more than half a million tonnes of raw sugar or about 50 percent of Moroccan consumption in 1996. ($1= 9.4 dirhams)
